justification: Explicitly labels the fillPendingConnectQueue body (355-362, lines 358-359) as the defect and states the precondition that fails to hold plus the exact assertion branch that surfaces it. Both ground-truth requirements are met.
claimed_lines: TestWebHdfsClientDeadlines.java:155-156 and :185-186 assertExceptionContains("...: connect timed out")
claimed_branches: non-blocking connect returns immediately and finishConnect() is never called, so the 129 iterations do not reliably fill the accept backlog before the WebHDFS call runs
because the backlog is not full when fs.listFiles/getDelegationToken runs, the client's connect succeeds and the 200 ms read timeout fires
control lands in catch (SocketTimeoutException) and the assertion requiring "connect timed out" fails with the observed AssertionError
gt_lines: TestWebHdfsTimeouts.consumeConnectionBacklog() body, pre-fix lines 355-362 (anonymized: TestWebHdfsClientDeadlines.fillPendingConnectQueue()) — the non-blocking SocketChannel connect loop that returns without confirming the accept queue is saturated; the fix appends a GenericTestUtils.waitFor probe (blocking connect with a 100 ms deadline, polling 100 ms up to 10 s) plus the failedToConsumeBacklog field / assumeBacklogConsumed()
the assumeBacklogConsumed() calls added inside the catch (SocketTimeoutException) blocks of testRedirectConnectTimeout (pre-fix line 216) and testTwoStepWriteConnectTimeout (pre-fix line 249)
gt_branches: the loop's only exit condition is the fixed count i < CLIENTS_TO_CONSUME_BACKLOG (129), not the state it stands for; combined with client.configureBlocking(false) the connect() calls only initiate handshakes, so the accept queue of new ServerSocket(0, CONNECTION_BACKLOG=1) can still have room when the helper returns

the connect-deadline checks then take the wrong arm: catch (SocketTimeoutException e) -> GenericTestUtils.assertExceptionContains(authority + ": connect timed out", e) receives a ": Read timed out" exception (or no exception at all -> fail("expected timeout"))
